auth.welcome_hint: Use the account your administrator issued.
auth.need_access: Need access or a password reset? Ask your system administrator.
auth.pillar_one_body: Bring finance, operations, people, and business data into one organized workspace.
auth.pillar_two_body: Business applications appear as each module is enabled for your organization.
auth.code_required: This account signs in with a second factor. Enter the code your authenticator app shows now.
auth.locked: Too many failed attempts. Wait fifteen minutes and try again.
auth.temporary_expired: The temporary password has expired. Ask an administrator for a new one.

about.report: Parameters over figures, with drill-down and export.
about.settings: The configuration this module's owner maintains.
about.inbox: Items addressed to you, acted on in place.

screen.nothing_unmatched_hint: Every line on this side has been accounted for.

purpose.finance_ap: What is owed to suppliers, and when it falls due

purpose.fixed_assets: The asset register, depreciation and disposal

purpose.reports: Figures across the business, with drill-down
purpose.master_data: The records every other module refers to

purpose.integrations: Interfaces, imports and the health of both

chart.title: Chart of Accounts
chart.subtitle: Manage account structure, classifications, and the financial hierarchy in one place.
chart.local_filter_note: These filters refine the accounts already loaded on this page. Search remains permission-controlled by the server.
chart.balance_unavailable_title: Balance data is not connected to this list
chart.balance_unavailable_body: No financial amount is estimated. Open the account record when its live ledger balance is available.
chart.no_account_selected_hint: Choose a row to see its structure and classification.
chart.journals_unavailable_title: No journal data in this workspace
chart.journals_unavailable_body: This front-end view does not widen the existing account query or request ledger entries.

preview.confirmation: Preview completed. No account data was saved.
preview.notice_body: This interaction demonstrates the requested interface only and makes no backend change.
preview.file_hint: The file stays on this device and is not uploaded.

chart.no_journals_yet: Nothing has been posted to this account yet.
chart.account_journal_hint: When transactions post to this account, they appear in Recent Journals and the General Ledger. The account master itself does not create a journal.
chart.group_journal_hint: Group accounts summarize their posting accounts; they do not accept direct journal entries.

dashboard.welcome_subtitle: Here's what's happening across your business today.
dashboard.presentation_note: This dashboard uses sample data for presentation.
dashboard.recent_activity_hint: The latest entries in the audit trail.
dashboard.no_reachable_pages: No pages are available within your permissions.
dashboard.your_access_hint: The screens your role may open.
dashboard.holds_need_reason: Stopped — reason required in my lane

shell.notifications_empty: You are all caught up. No new notifications.
shell.search_placeholder: Search screens… (type a page or module name)
shell.search_hint: ↑ ↓ to move · Enter to open · Esc to close · Ctrl K opens from anywhere
shell.interface_style_hint: Choose an optional layout. Your current theme colors stay in place.
shell.appearance_save_idle: Changes save to your account automatically.
shell.appearance_save_error: Could not save. Check your connection and try again.

documents.subtitle: Organize files, templates, approvals, and document workspaces in one secure place.
documents.preview_notice: These actions demonstrate the interface and do not save or upload files.
documents.workspaces_hint: Open the tools available to your role.
documents.recent_empty_hint: Documents you open or upload will appear here once live document data is connected.

admin.reason_placeholder: Why — this is kept in the audit trail
admin.history_empty: Nothing has been recorded for this record yet.
admin.name: Name
admin.code_hint: Letters, digits, hyphens or underscores. Cannot be changed later.

company.title: Company Setup
company.subtitle: The legal entity every module works for. One company; saved here, read everywhere.
company.not_set: The company has not been set up yet. Fill in the details below to create the main company record.
company.base_currency_hint: The ledger keeps its books in this currency. Other currencies are priced through Master Data → Currencies and Rates.
company.address_hint: Head office address as it appears on documents.
company.main_branch_hint: The first branch is the head office. Other branches are added later under Master Data → Branches.
company.appearance_hint: Each user chooses and saves an individual appearance in their profile.
company.accent_hint: The highlight colour — the buttons, the selected row, the mark under a title.
company.appearance_profile_hint: Your appearance is saved to your account and follows you across devices. Each user chooses independently.

branches.title: Branches
branches.subtitle: Every user and every transaction belongs to a branch. A branch is never deleted — it is deactivated.
branches.created_note: Creating a branch also creates its main warehouse. Choose a company bank or cash account on each payment or receipt.

departments.title: Departments
departments.subtitle: Departments route approvals: a document goes to the manager of the department it was raised in.
departments.members_empty: Nobody is scoped to this department yet.
departments.add_member_hint: Scopes the person to this department. Tick the box to make them its manager.

users.title: Users
users.subtitle: Each employee has an individual account, scoped to the branches and departments they work in.
users.temp_password_note: Shown once. Hand it to the person; they will be asked to replace it at first sign-in.
users.reset_password_hint: Issues a new temporary password and signs the person out everywhere.
users.deactivate_hint: Every live session ends immediately. The account stays in history.
users.mailed: The temporary password has been e-mailed to {email}.
users.mail_failed: The e-mail could not be sent; the temporary password is shown below instead.
users.also_employee_hint: Ticked, the person is put in HR with the account, linked to it, in the default branch. Untick for a sign-in that is not a person on the staff.

managers.title: Department Managers
managers.subtitle: Who finalises what. A manager approves documents raised in their own department without a second approval.
managers.empty: No department has a manager yet. Assign one from the department's page.

roles.title: Roles
roles.subtitle: A role is a named set of permissions. People hold roles; roles hold grants.
roles.grants_hint: Tick the actions this role may take on each system section. What is not ticked is refused.
roles.system_note: A system role keeps its code and name; its permissions can still be changed.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.subtitle: Choose a role, then tick what it may see and do in every system section. What is not ticked is hidden from the navigation and refused by URL.
permissions.legend: Verbs are shown by their first letters; hover for the full name.
permissions.effect: What is ticked is what this role sees in the navigation and may open by URL; what is not ticked is refused on both.
permissions.how_body: A role is a set of ticks. A person holds one or more roles; they can do exactly what their roles tick, nothing else. "View" on a section puts it in their navigation and lets the URL open; without it the item is hidden and the URL is refused. Approval routing uses "Approve" together with the Department Manager flag on the department (Settings → Department Managers). Super users bypass all of this.

verb_help.view: Shows the section in the navigation and lets its pages open — by menu or by URL. Without it the section does not exist for this role.
verb_help.create: Lets the role add new records in the section.
verb_help.edit_draft: Lets the role change a record while it is still a draft. Approved records are not editable.
verb_help.submit: Lets the role send a draft for approval. The document goes to the manager of the department it was raised in.
verb_help.approve: Lets the role approve or reject what was submitted. A Department Manager finalises documents of their own department without a second approval.
verb_help.execute: Lets the role carry out an approved document (e.g. issue stock, pay).
verb_help.post: Lets the role post to the ledger.
verb_help.reverse_cancel: Lets the role reverse or cancel a record, with a reason kept in the audit trail. Nothing is ever deleted.
verb_help.print: Lets the role print the record.
verb_help.export: Lets the role export the list as a file. Every export is recorded in the audit trail.
verb_help.import: Lets the role bring records in from a file.
verb_help.configure: Lets the role edit settings of the section (names, assignments, defaults).
verb_help.administer: Lets the role deactivate, reset and administer — the highest level for the section.

jobs.title: Background Jobs
jobs.subtitle: The scheduled jobs the server runs, with their last run; and the hand-offs waiting to be delivered. Read-only: a job is run from the server (scripts/ops/run-job.sh).
jobs.no_crontab: The crontab (scripts/ops/crontab.erp) is not beside this build; nothing is scheduled.

backup_health.title: Backup and Health
backup_health.subtitle: What /healthz answers, what the daily health check found, and the backup sets on disk. The same checks notify the accounting managers each morning.
backup_health.no_backups: No backup set has been written under {root}. Install the crontab (scripts/ops/install-cron.sh) and read docs/RUNBOOK-database-recovery.md.

numbering.title: Numbering
numbering.subtitle: Every document takes its number from a series. Numbers are never reused; gaps are kept, not filled.
numbering.recent_empty: This series has not issued a number yet.

audit.title: Audit Trail
audit.subtitle: Who did what, when, to which record, and whether it succeeded. Append-only; nothing here can be edited.
audit.search_placeholder: Search by action, record or person
audit.former_record: a record that no longer exists

approvals.title: My Approvals
approvals.subtitle: Documents waiting for your decision, then what you submitted and what you decided.
approvals.inbox_empty: Nothing is waiting for your approval.
approvals.my_submissions_empty: You have not submitted anything yet.
approvals.my_decisions_empty: You have not decided anything yet.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.unreadable: The {band} section could not be read. Everything else on this page is unaffected.
dashboard.unidentified_receipts: {count, plural, one {# receipt has no payer and cannot settle anything} other {# receipts have no payer and cannot settle anything}}
dashboard.account_without_ledger: {code} has no G/L account behind it and cannot post.
dashboard.chart_trading: Income and expenses, month by month

admin.rows_shown: {count, plural, =0 {No records} one {# record} other {# records}}
admin.code_auto_hint: Left blank, it is made from the name. It cannot be changed later.

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.hint: Up to 25MB. Programs and archives are refused on their content, not their name.

journals.title: Journal Entries
journals.subtitle: Entries raised here, and where each one has got to.
journals.posting_date_hint: The date it hits the books; it decides the period.
journals.currency_hint: The currency the amount is in. An account tied to one currency sets this itself.
journals.department_hint: Which department the cost or income belongs to.
journals.unbalanced_detail: Debits come to {debit} and credits to {credit}. It cannot be posted until they agree.
journals.reverse_confirm_body: You are about to reverse {entryNo}. This creates a linked journal entry that offsets it. This action cannot be undone. Are you sure you want to continue?
journals.reverse_hint: A posted entry is never edited. Reversing it writes the opposite entry and links the two.
journals.not_in_finance: You are not in a Finance department, so you cannot raise an entry yet. An administrator adds a department with "Finance department" ticked, then adds you to it.
journals.discard_confirm: {entryNo} and its lines will be removed. This cannot be undone, and the number is not given to another entry.
journals.rate_note: The rate is the one in force on the posting date; it is set in Currencies and Rates, never here.
journals.no_attachments_posted: No attachments were found on this entry when it was posted.
journals.audit_subtitle: Everything recorded about {entryNo}: who did what, and when.

reversals.title: Reversals
reversals.subtitle: Every correction made to the books, and why.

periods.title: Accounting periods
periods.subtitle: The months the books are open for.
periods.year_hint: Twelve monthly periods are created between these dates.
periods.none: No year has been opened yet.
periods.none_detail: Nothing can be posted until a year exists — open one to begin.
periods.change_hint: Closing a period stops posting into it. Soft closed still allows an approved adjustment.
periods.reason_hint: Kept in the audit trail beside the change.
periods.close_checks_pass: {period} may be closed: every blocking check passes as at {asOf}. Warnings, if any, are recorded with the close.
periods.close_checks_fail: {period} cannot be closed: {count, plural, one {# blocking check fails} other {# blocking checks fail}}. Open each line to see the figure on its own screen.
periods.check_gl_integrity: General ledger integrity (unbalanced or orphaned postings)
periods.check_unposted_journals: Journals dated in the period not yet posted
periods.check_stock_ledger_integrity: Stock ledger agrees with its documents and layers
periods.check_stock_documents_waiting: Stock documents dated in the period still waiting
periods.check_inventory_value_equals_gl: Inventory value (layers) equals the inventory accounts — now
periods.check_negative_stock: Positions below zero (goods still at sea) — now
periods.check_bank_reconciled: Every bank account reconciled to the period end
periods.check_fx_rate_current: A USD rate dated within the period
periods.check_project_recognition: Revenue recognised for every running customer project

reports.does_not_balance: The two sides do not agree
reports.nothing_posted: Nothing was posted in this period.
reports.trial_balance_subtitle: Every account with a movement, and the two totals that must agree.
reports.gl_subtitle: Every account and its balance. Press an account to see the journals posted to it.
reports.as_at_hint: The Balance Sheet is drawn at this date.
reports.result_for_the_period: Result to date (not yet closed to retained earnings)
reports.no_accounts: There are no posting accounts yet.
reports.currency_hint: IQD is the ledger. USD reads the same postings at the rate that applied when each one posted.
reports.level_hint: Level 1 shows only the headers; each further level opens what is beneath them.
reports.income_statement_subtitle: What was earned and spent between the two dates.
reports.balance_sheet_subtitle: What is owned and owed at the date, with the result under Equity.
reports.changes_in_equity_subtitle: What equity stood at, what moved it, and what it stands at now.
reports.cash_flow_subtitle: Where the cash came from and where it went, read from the journals that moved it.
reports.nothing_in_equity: No equity account has been posted to.
reports.opening_cash: Cash at the start of the period
reports.closing_cash: Cash at the end of the period
reports.cash_reconciles: The movement agrees with the cash balances
reports.cash_does_not_reconcile: The movement does not agree with the cash balances
reports.cash_not_configured: No account has been marked as cash yet — set one on the Cash Flow mapping, or this statement has nothing to explain.
reports.no_cash_moved: No cash moved in this period.
reports.inflow_hint: Money in is positive; money out is negative.
reports.nothing_in_stock: No stock is held in any warehouse.
reports.as_it_stands: Stock held now, valued at what it cost
reports.units_and_value: Quantity is in units. Total Price is what that stock cost in IQD (FIFO), not a quantity and not a selling price.

accounts.parent_hint: Where it sits. Only a header account — marked [+] — can hold sub-accounts.
accounts.name: Name
accounts.kind_hint: A header groups other accounts; a posting account takes entries.
accounts.deactivate_hint: It stays in the system and on old entries; it simply stops accepting new ones.
accounts.no_parent: There is no header account to hang this under yet.
accounts.sub_accounts_hint: This is a posting account, so nothing can hang beneath it. It can become a header — but only while it has never been posted to, because a header carries no balance of its own.
accounts.is_a_header: This is a header account. Create an account under it from the Chart of Accounts.
accounts.header_no_line: A header account takes no mapping.
accounts.cash_flow_inside_net_income: This account is already inside Net Income, the first figure of the Cash Flow Statement. An expense that has not been paid is added back through the liability it is owed on — map Salaries Payable or Accounts Payable, not the expense itself.
accounts.control_hint: Choose which subledger this account controls. Customer and supplier control accounts feed their statements. Changes affect future postings; existing journals and statements are not rewritten.

rates.title: Accounting rates
rates.subtitle: The rates every posting is measured at.
rates.rate_hint: How many {ledger} one unit is worth.
rates.effective_hint: It applies from this date until a later rate supersedes it. The earliest rate also covers anything posted before it.
rates.none: No rate has been published yet.
rates.none_detail: Every entry is measured in the ledger currency and in USD, so nothing can be posted until a USD rate covers {date}.
rates.decimals_hint: Digits after the point when amounts are shown.
rates.symbol_hint: Optional — €, £, ₺. Shown in lists; amounts still format by code.
rates.in_force_hint: What each currency is measured at today, {date} — the most recent rate that had taken effect. This is the figure a journal posted now would use.
rates.none_in_force: No rate has taken effect yet.
rates.also_published_hint: On record and not cancelled, but not what applies today.
rates.add_currency_note: A currency has to exist here before a rate can be published for it, or an account held in it.

cost_centres.subtitle: Where cost is gathered, independently of who reports to whom.
cost_centres.created_note: The code follows the name unless you type one. It is quoted by every posting that carries this cost centre, so it does not change afterwards.
cost_centres.owner_hint: Budget responsibility rests with a person, not a box.
cost_centres.branch_hint: Leave blank for a cost centre that is not tied to one branch.

uom.subtitle: The units items state their quantities in.
uom.created_note: Keep the list short. PCS, PC and PIECE are three units as far as every later report is concerned.
uom.code_is_fixed: The code cannot change — it would restate every quantity ever recorded against it.
uom.no_items: No item uses this unit yet.
uom.in_use_warning: This unit is the base unit of {count} item(s) and cannot be retired until they name another.

payment_terms.subtitle: When an invoice falls due, and what an early settlement is worth.
payment_terms.created_note: The code follows the name unless you type one. Instalments are set on the record page.
payment_terms.basis_hint: The date the clock starts on.
payment_terms.due_days_hint: For a term that falls due once. Ignored when instalments are set.
payment_terms.discount_hint: Both a percentage and a number of days, or neither.
payment_terms.instalments_hint: Leave every row blank for a term that falls due once. When rows are used they must total 100% — otherwise part of each invoice would never fall due.
payment_terms.no_partners: No partner uses these terms yet.

payment_methods.subtitle: How money is received and paid — cash, transfer, cheque.
payment_methods.created_note: The method is what a person picks. The kind beneath it is the rail the money moves on.
payment_methods.kind_hint: A cheque is a bank method: it clears through a bank account and reconciles against a statement.
payment_methods.fee_hint: A percentage of the amount. Leave blank when the method costs nothing.
payment_methods.fee_account_hint: Required when a fee is charged — a fee with nowhere to post is a cost nobody accounts for.
payment_methods.confirmation_hint: What the accountant enters when the payment is confirmed: a SWIFT copy and MT103 reference, a transfer reference, a signed cash voucher, or a cheque number.

accounts_shared.gl_hint: Cash and bank balances are assets. Choose an active, approved posting account that no other bank or cash account uses.
accounts_shared.gl_missing: No G/L account — the account it named is gone. Choose one.
accounts_shared.currency_hint: Three letters. The account can only hold this currency.
accounts_shared.approval_limit_hint: The ceiling a payment from this account may reach.
accounts_shared.transfers_in: Moved in from our own accounts
accounts_shared.transfers_out: Moved out to our own accounts

bank_accounts.subtitle: The company’s bank accounts, and the G/L account each is carried in.
bank_accounts.created_note: The G/L account must be an unused, active, approved posting account under Assets. The ERP code is generated; enter the actual account number assigned by the bank.
bank_accounts.number_hint: Enter the actual number assigned by the bank. It identifies this bank account on statements; the ERP account code is generated separately.
bank_accounts.statement_format_hint: How its statements arrive, so they can be imported.
bank_accounts.bank_hint: From the Banks list. The name below is filled from it when left blank.

cash_accounts.subtitle: The company’s cash floats, who holds each one, and the G/L account it is carried in.
cash_accounts.created_note: A cash account needs a custodian. A float that is nobody’s responsibility cannot be counted.
cash_accounts.custodian_hint: The person answerable for this float at a cash count.
cash_accounts.cash_limit_hint: The most this float may hold.

items.subtitle: The one item record Purchasing, Inventory and Sales all use.
items.created_note: The system gives the item its code when you save. It is the identity every document selects by, and it does not change afterwards.
items.kind_hint: A service has no stock, so it tracks nothing.
items.new_category_hint: Typed here, this wins over the list above.
items.tracking_hint: A stock item must track serial numbers, batch numbers or both. Ignored for a service.
items.sales_account_hint: A matching scoped posting exception wins first. If none matches, this item account is used; when it is blank, the general sales mapping is the fallback.
items.purchase_account_hint: Where a purchase of this item posts, unless a rule says otherwise.
items.no_suppliers: No supplier is linked yet, so this item cannot be ordered.
items.no_more_suppliers: Every supplier is already linked to this item.
items.supplier_item_code_hint: The code this supplier knows the item by — read from here rather than typed on an order.
items.prices_hint: Defaults per base unit. Invoice prices are copied into drafts; changing a default does not change saved invoices.
items.no_stock: None on hand. Nothing has been received into stock for this item yet.
items.stock_hint: Counted from stock movements — receipts add, deliveries and issues take away — so it always agrees with what actually moved.
items.inventory_account_hint: Where this item’s stock is held. Debited when bought, credited when sold.
items.cogs_account_hint: What this item costs when it is sold.
items.unit_holds_hint: How many {base} one of this unit holds — 24 for a carton of 24, 0.5 for half.
items.base_unit_hint: The unit its stock is counted in. Other units (a carton, a roll) are added on the item.
items.units_hint: Stock is counted in {base}; a line in another unit is converted at the movement, exactly, or refused.

partners.subtitle_customer: Who we sell to. One record per company, whatever else they are to us.
partners.subtitle_supplier: Who we buy from. One record per company, whatever else they are to us.
partners.subtitle_all: Every company we deal with, customer or supplier or both.
partners.created_note_customer: If this company is already a supplier, use the same code — it will be given the customer role rather than a second record.
partners.created_note_supplier: If this company is already a customer, use the same code — it will be given the supplier role rather than a second record.
partners.trade_name_hint: The name they are known by, when it differs from the registered one.
partners.credit_limit_hint: What they may owe at once.
partners.statement_subtitle_customer: What each customer owes. Sales are Debit; receipts and credits are Credit.
partners.statement_subtitle_supplier: What is owed to each supplier. Purchases are Credit; payments and credits are Debit.
partners.statement_choose_customer: Choose a customer to read their account.
partners.statement_choose_supplier: Choose a supplier to read their account.
partners.statement_empty: Nothing posted to this account in the period.
partners.statement_party_unknown: No {side} matches that. Type a code or a name, or pick one from the list.
partners.statement_party_ambiguous: That could be more than one {side}. Type more of the code or the name.

mapping.subtitle: The lines each report prints.
mapping.name: Name
mapping.kind_subtotal: Total — adds up the lines above it

invoices.save_failed: The line could not be saved. Your changes are still here; leave the row again to retry.
invoices.resize_column: Drag to resize this column; double-click to reset it
invoices.availability_hint: Availability is checked again when posting.
invoices.accounts_hint: Leave blank to use the configured mapping.
invoices.reverse_hint: Undoes the posting: the journal is reversed, the stock goes back to where it came from at the cost it left at, and the invoice is marked reversed. Refused while a payment, return or credit memo rests on it.
invoices.account_missing: The account this invoice names no longer exists — choose one in Chart of Accounts.

ap_invoices.title: Purchase Invoices
ap_invoices.subtitle: What the company has been billed
ap_invoices.line_hint: Leave a row blank to skip it.

ar_invoices.title: Sales Invoices
ar_invoices.subtitle: What the company has billed
ar_invoices.line_hint: Leave a row blank to skip it.
ar_invoices.account_selection_hint: For saved, unposted lines: a matching scoped mapping, then the item sales account, then the general mapping. Posting checks the setup again.
ar_invoices.posted_accounts_hint: These accounts are recorded on the original journal. Later setup changes do not rewrite posted history.
ar_invoices.revenue_trace_missing: Historical revenue-account details are unavailable. No account has been inferred from current setup; review the original journal.
ar_invoices.adjustment_hint: Adjustments are separate journals. Draft adjustments do not affect balances.

sales_returns.title: Sales Returns
sales_returns.subtitle: Goods a customer has sent back
sales_returns.pick_invoice: Choose the invoice being returned against.
sales_returns.partner_optional: Optional — narrows the invoices suggested below.
sales_returns.invoice_hint: Invoice number, or part of it
sales_returns.invoice_ambiguous: That could be more than one invoice. Type more of its number.

goods_returns.title: Purchase Returns
goods_returns.subtitle: Goods sent back to a supplier
goods_returns.pick_invoice: Choose the invoice being returned against.
goods_returns.partner_optional: Optional — narrows the invoices suggested below.
goods_returns.invoice_hint: Invoice number, or part of it
goods_returns.invoice_ambiguous: That could be more than one invoice. Type more of its number.

supplier_payments.title: Payments
supplier_payments.subtitle: Money paid to suppliers
supplier_payments.no_accounts: Set up a bank or cash account first.
supplier_payments.allocate_after_create: Invoices are allocated on the payment’s own page, once it is created.

customer_receipts.title: Receipts
customer_receipts.subtitle: Money received from customers
customer_receipts.no_accounts: Set up a bank or cash account first.
customer_receipts.allocate_after_create: Invoices are allocated on the receipt’s own page, once it is posted.

in_transit.title: Invoice Status Tracking
in_transit.subtitle: Goods bought abroad, between the invoice and the shelf
in_transit.no_warehouse_for_stage: No warehouse is set for the next stage.
in_transit.notify_title: Notify these users when a status changes
in_transit.containers_note: Imports are tracked container by container from their B/L; this page keeps the shipments of invoices that are not imports.

setup.no_active_customers: {count} customer(s) exist and none is active. Reactivate one on the Customers screen.
setup.no_active_suppliers: {count} supplier(s) exist and none is active. Reactivate one on the Suppliers screen.
setup.no_active_items: {count} item(s) exist and none is a stock item that is active. Check them on the Items screen.
setup.no_accounts: Set up a bank or cash account first.
setup.no_active_accounts: {count} bank or cash account(s) exist and none is active.

posting_mappings.subtitle: Which account each document posts to. The posting engine never chooses one on its own (§3.3).
posting_mappings.not_eligible_hint: The saved account is not eligible for this line. Check its approval, active status and control-account designation.
posting_mappings.control_hint: Only accounts designated as a {kind} control account are offered here. Set the designation in Chart of Accounts.
posting_mappings.missing: {count, plural, one {One required line has no account} other {# required lines have no account}}
posting_mappings.complete: Every required line has an account

transfers.subtitle: Items moved from one warehouse to another
transfers.created_note: The system gives the transfer its number. The stock leaves the first warehouse and arrives in the second at the cost it already carries.
transfers.ledger_missing_hint: This transfer has no rows in the Stock Movement ledger, so it moved nothing the system can see. It is a remnant of data that was removed outside the application; report it rather than re-entering it.

reconciliation.subtitle: Bring the system's quantity to what is on the shelf
reconciliation.created_note: In adds stock that was found; Out removes stock that is missing. The system gives the reconciliation its number.
reconciliation.by_journal: Posted by journal — open the statement
reconciliation.owed_total: Net position — agrees with the statement

opening_stock.subtitle: The stock the company starts with
opening_stock.created_note: The system gives the document its number. Save sends it for approval; approval brings the stock in.
opening_stock.awaiting: Waiting for approval by someone other than the person who entered it.

integrity.title: The stock ledger disagrees with its documents in {count} place(s).
integrity.hint: The figures on this screen are read from the ledger; until this is resolved, one of them is not what the documents say. Tell the accounting manager.

stock_ledger.subtitle: One item, warehouse by warehouse: opening, every movement, closing
stock_ledger.choose_item: Choose an item to read its ledger. Every row is a document; the number opens it.
stock_ledger.none: No movements of {item} in this range.

stock_movements.subtitle: Every movement of stock, In or Out

admin.minted_code_note: The system gives it its code when you save. The code cannot be typed or changed.

treasury_reporting.subtitle: Every bank and cash account, and what its balance is made of
treasury_reporting.no_accounts: No bank or cash accounts are set up yet.
treasury_reporting.no_movements: Nothing moved in this account over this period.

open_items.subtitle_customer: What customers owe, invoice by invoice, and how late it is
open_items.subtitle_supplier: What we owe suppliers, invoice by invoice, and how late it is
open_items.party_placeholder: Everybody — or type a name or code
open_items.nothing: Nothing matches — no invoice is outstanding for this date.

statement_outstanding.title: Invoice Balances
statement_outstanding.nothing: Nothing here — no invoice on this account matches what is being shown.

payables.title: Import applications
payables.subtitle: One record per import — from the supplier's invoice to the warehouse
payables.amount_hint: Leave empty when the lines carry prices.
payables.lines_hint: For goods, the PI lines become the purchase order — item, quantity, price.
payables.link_invoice_hint: The invoice id of a posted invoice of this supplier.
payables.detail_hint: Required for OTHER — say what is actually wrong.
payables.edit_lines: Edit PI lines (supersedes — the old lines stay in the record)
payables.no_receipts: No confirmations yet — the benefiting department raises one from Service Receipts.

payables_settings.title: Payables Settings
payables_settings.subtitle: Types, stages, time limits, reason codes — configuration, not code
payables_settings.name: Name
payables_settings.new_limit: Set a limit (a change is a new dated row)

payables_contracts.title: Recurring Contracts
payables_contracts.subtitle: The standing commitments — rent, utilities, subscriptions — each raising its own payable, period by period.
payables_contracts.auto_confirm: Auto-confirm each period (the contract is its own evidence)
payables_contracts.invoice_expected: An invoice is expected each period
payables_contracts.amend_amount_hint: Leave empty to keep the amount; future periods only.

payables_receipts.title: Service Receipts
payables_receipts.subtitle: Did we actually get it? The benefiting department's confirmations, before anything is paid.

payables_orders.title: Purchase Orders
payables_orders.subtitle: The commitments: what was ordered, what has arrived, what has been billed.

payables_goods.title: Goods Receipts
payables_goods.subtitle: What arrived, against which order, into which warehouse.

expenses.name: Name
expenses.name_hint: What it is for, as it should read in the list — e.g. "Erbil office rent — October".
expenses.reference_hint: Transfer reference, cheque number or cash voucher number.
expenses.note_hint: What is happening with this bill — e.g. "landlord travelling, pays Monday".
expenses.is_import_hint: This is an import — open the import application behind it

payment_applications.subtitle: The company’s requests to its banks and cashier to pay a supplier — longest waiting first.
payment_applications.new_note: Choose the import. Its page opens with the payment dialog, beside its instalments and what is already applied.
payment_applications.none_for_import: Nothing asked of the bank yet.
payment_applications.payee_hint: Required for SWIFT and transfers; it must be verified on the supplier before the file goes to the bank.
payment_applications.bank_reference_hint: The bank’s file or application number, if it gives one.
payment_applications.send_note: The checks run again with today’s figures. The clock starts on the date the file went.
payment_applications.override_hint: Failing now: {checks}. As a manager you may send anyway — the reason is kept on the application and in the status log.
payment_applications.confirm_posts_payment: Confirming posts a supplier payment dated this day and allocates it to {invoices}. The reservation is released.
payment_applications.confirm_posts_advance: No invoice of this import is posted yet, so confirming posts a supplier advance (a deposit) against its purchase order, dated this day. The reservation is released.
payment_applications.attach_copy_hint: Attach the SWIFT copy or the signed voucher below, after confirming.
payment_applications.debit_note: The date the bank statement shows the money leaving. A reconciliation match records it by itself.
payment_applications.no_instalments: No instalments planned — plan the terms to pay against them.
payment_applications.plan_note: The instalments total {amount}. A percentage is of the whole; the last row takes the rounding. Instalments already applied stay as they are.
payment_applications.loan_hint: When the funding source is a bank loan: the loan, its account and what it has left to fund.
payment_applications.confirm_before_cut_over_note: For an application migrated from the sheet whose money left before the cut-over: the SWIFT date and reference from the bank’s copy are recorded and nothing is posted — that payment is already in the books the ERP opened with. Money that left after the cut-over is confirmed with the button beside this one, which posts it.
payment_applications.exchange_open: Fully paid in its currency; in dinars its invoices still owe {owed} and its payments are {over} over them. That is the exchange difference: it is booked once the exchange gain and loss are mapped on Posting Mappings.

supplier_advances.subtitle: Money paid to a supplier before the invoice — the deposits on imports, and advances against orders.
supplier_advances.new_note: An advance is paid against a purchase order the company has committed to. The supplier comes from the order.
supplier_advances.no_settlements: Not yet set against an invoice.

banks.subtitle: The banks the company holds accounts with — Mansour, Arab, NBI, Rafidain and any other.
banks.created_note: A bank is named once and its accounts point to it. A time limit can be set per bank.
banks.swift_hint: 8 or 11 characters, e.g. MBIVIQBAXXX. Leave blank if not known yet.
banks.no_accounts: No company account is held with this bank yet.

customs_pd.subtitle: The customs pre-declarations (ASYCUDA), the soonest to expire first.
customs_pd.register_note: The PD number, dates and bank exactly as the ASYCUDA screen shows them. Several PDs per import are allowed.
customs_pd.pd_no_hint: The ASYCUDA number, as customs issued it.
customs_pd.expiry_hint: As ASYCUDA shows it — the validity is the customs office’s, not computed.
customs_pd.applied_n: {count} PD statuses updated from the ASYCUDA list.
customs_pd.none_for_import: No PD registered for this import yet.
customs_pd.other_years: The same number was also registered in:
customs_pd.reregister_note: The new PD supersedes {pdNo}; {pdNo} stays exactly as customs left it.
customs_pd.asycuda_subtitle: Paste the document list from ASYCUDA. Nothing changes until you have seen the difference and applied it.
customs_pd.asycuda_hint: One PD per line: the number, the status as ASYCUDA writes it, and the date if shown — separated by tabs, commas or spaces.
customs_pd.asycuda_nothing: No line could be matched to a PD.
customs_pd.link_note: PD {pdNo} came from the sheet without an import it could be matched to. Name the import it belongs to; it carries the PD from then on, with its status as it stands. A linked PD is not unlinked.
customs_pd.view_holding: Holding list — not linked to an import

shipments.subtitle: The bills of lading of every import, each with its containers counted as they arrive.
shipments.containers_subtitle: Every container on its own — where it is, how late, what it carries, where it was received.
shipments.new_bl_note: Enter the B/L as the shipping line issued it and paste its container numbers. A B/L may carry part of an import; an import may have any number of B/Ls.
shipments.containers_hint: Paste the container numbers from the B/L — one per line, or separated by commas. MSCU1234565.
shipments.spread_lines: Spread the import's lines equally over these containers (estimated — the warehouse confirms)
shipments.none_for_import: Not shipped yet — no B/L recorded.
shipments.move_all_note: Every container of this B/L that has not reached the stage moves to it, each with its own history row.
shipments.variance_hint: Required when anything is short, damaged or different from the plan — it opens the claim for purchasing.
shipments.estimated_note: Spread equally from the B/L — confirm what the container actually carries.
shipments.receive_note: Count what came off the container. The goods move from transit into the warehouse at the cost the invoice gave them.
shipments.load_plan_note: Each model in this container and how many. Saving replaces the plan; the old one is kept in the history.
shipments.no_plan: No plan yet — enter what the container carries.

loans.subtitle: Every bank loan in one register: what it lends, what it costs, what it funded and what is still owed.
loans.new_note: Enter the bank's offer as its letter states it. The schedule is generated at once and can be retyped until the loan is approved.
loans.commission_amount_hint: Blank for principal × %; type the bank's figure when it rounds.
loans.capitalised: Capitalise the commission into the imports the loan funds
loans.interest_hint: Blank when the loan carries none.
loans.custom_dates_hint: For a custom schedule: one date per line (YYYY-MM-DD).
loans.disburse_note: Posts the disbursement: the account receives {net}; the loan liability is {principal}.
loans.pay_note: Instalments are repaid in order. Posts Dr loan liability (principal), interest and commission, Cr the bank account, dated the day it was paid.
loans.pay_commission_note: Posts the commission the bank charged on its own: Dr the funded imports' cost (or commission expense), Cr the bank account.
loans.edit_schedule_note: One row per instalment: due date, principal, interest and — for a spread commission — its share. The principal must total {principal}.
loans.none_funded: Nothing drawn on this loan yet.

landed_cost.none: No cost charged to this import yet.
landed_cost.add_note: A charge comes from a posted document: name the journal that parked the cost on the clearing account. A forwarder's invoice line charged to this import and a loan's commission arrive here by themselves.
landed_cost.withdraw_note: Only a charge from a journal, not yet locked, is withdrawn. A charge that came with its document goes when the document is reversed.
landed_cost.lock_note: Allocates {total} over the stock the containers brought in. What is still on hand takes it into its unit cost; what is already sold takes it to cost of sales. Posts Dr Inventory / Cost of sales, Cr the clearing account.
landed_cost.manual_hint: Manual only: the amount each model carries; they must add up to the charges.
landed_cost.not_lockable: The landed cost is locked once every PD is totally written off (§20.1, condition 3).

employees.title: Employees
employees.subtitle: One record per person: who works here, where, and every dated change of place, manager and status. Salary rows sit under their own grant.
employees.move_hint: Leave a field as it is to keep it. The change takes effect from the date given and is kept as history.
employees.end_hint: The employee keeps their record and history; they can no longer be named as a manager.
employees.link_user_hint: A linked person sees their own record read-only. Choose the blank entry to unlink.
employees.compensation_hint: A change is a new dated row; the previous row stays.

organisation.title: Organisation
organisation.subtitle: The tree as it stands in the rows: each department, its positions in reporting order, who holds each. Headcount is a count.

hr_settings.title: HR Settings
hr_settings.subtitle: Positions, pay components, leave types and working calendars — rows the HR manager edits. Nothing deletes; a row is deactivated.

legacy_import.subtitle: The old system's ten workbooks into the ERP, once: dry run first, read the report, then apply. Partners, items and warehouses are created where missing; the partners' balances post as the opening position; the stock is raised for costing and approval; every old document is kept as history.
legacy_import.run_note: Choose all the workbooks the old system exported (customers, suppliers, account balances, materials, warehouses, sales, purchases, receipt vouchers, payment vouchers, the accounts). Each is recognised by its header, not its name — except that the suppliers' file must have “Supplier” or “مورد” in its name. A dry run writes nothing but its report; apply is refused for a set that has not been dry-run, and a re-run adds only what is missing.
legacy_import.cut_over_hint: The day the old books close: the opening journal and the opening stock carry this date. The period must be open.
legacy_import.stops_none: Nothing — the set can be applied.
legacy_import.problems_title: Rows that could not be read
legacy_import.partners_create: To be created: {count} · already there: {matched} · name disagrees: {conflicts}
legacy_import.balances_note: Posted at the cut-over as one journal per currency, in dinars: each partner on its control account, debit when they owe us and credit when we owe them, the equity side balancing. The dollar accounts are converted at the rate the old books carried them at ({implied}); the ERP's own rate on the cut-over date is {erp} — set it to the same figure on Finance → Exchange Rates and the USD reading of every statement is the old one to the cent.
legacy_import.totals_title: Totals against the old trial balance
legacy_import.agrees: The partner balances agree with the old trial balance to the dinar.
legacy_import.disagrees: The partner balances do not agree with the old trial balance — check the files before applying.
legacy_import.stock_note: One Opening Stock document per warehouse, submitted and not approved: the quantities are the old books', the unit costs are the latest the old books carry (the newest purchase, else the newest sale's cost). The old trial balance values the stock at {tb}; the proposed costs come to {proposed}. Correct the costs on the Opening Stock screen, then approve — nothing posts until then.
legacy_import.no_cost_title: Positions with no known cost (raised at zero)
legacy_import.in_transit_title: Sold, still at sea — not stock
legacy_import.in_transit_note: Negative quantities and the in-transit warehouse are goods sold before they arrived (the accountant, 2026-10-02). They are not imported as stock; tie them up with the open import applications.
legacy_import.archive_note: Every old sale line, purchase line, receipt and payment is kept as read-only history on the partner it names. Nothing in it posts: the opening balances already carry the net position.
legacy_import.unmatched_names: Names in the sales or purchases that match no partner (kept by name): {names}
legacy_import.unmatched_codes: Voucher account numbers that match no partner (kept by number): {codes}
legacy_import.tb_title: The old trial balance — for the opening journal you enter by hand
legacy_import.tb_note: Cash boxes, exchange centres, paid capital, and the year's expenses and revenues are not partners: enter them as an opening journal on Finance → Journals, dated the cut-over, so the ERP's balance sheet starts where the old one ended.
legacy_import.history_none: No documents from the old books.

payables_migration.subtitle: QS_DASHBOARD.xlsx into the Payables module, once: dry run first, read the report, apply, and have the cleared comparison signed off.
payables_migration.run_note: A dry run writes nothing but its report. Apply is refused for a file that has not been dry-run, and a re-run adds only what is missing. Suppliers are matched by name and never created; match them on the supplier records and run again.
payables_migration.no_account: None — open one, then run again
payables_migration.holding_title: PDs with no import — the customs officer's holding list
payables_migration.verify_title: Verify the SWIFT date — not paid in the sheet, PD totally written off
payables_migration.cleared_title: Cleared — the sheet's "Clear?" against the rule (§20.1)
payables_migration.cleared_counts: The rule clears {rule}; the sheet marked {legacy}. Marked cleared but the PD is not written off: {marked}. PD written off but not marked: {written}.
payables_migration.no_differences: The sheet and the rule agree on every import.
payables_migration.sign_off_hint: Signed off by an accountant who did not apply the import.
payables_migration.invalid_containers: Numbers that are not container numbers
payables_migration.estimated_bls: B/Ls whose quantity was spread over their containers (estimated): {count}
payables_migration.fixes_title: Values changed on the way in
payables_migration.shipments: Four-stage shipments migrated: {migrated} ({created} new imports, {linked} linked)
payables_migration.skip_no_dashboard_row: No dashboard row has this PO / invoice number.
payables_migration.skip_no_swift_method: No SWIFT payment method is set up.

whatsapp.title: WhatsApp
whatsapp.subtitle: The bridge on the company number, who may be reached and who may ask, which notifications reach a phone, the limits, and every message in and out. Read-only from chat; nothing deletes.
whatsapp.bridge_note: The bridge is a separate process (npm run whatsapp-bridge, or the systemd service on the server). On first start it prints a QR code to scan from the company phone: WhatsApp → Linked devices → Link a device. It delivers the whatsapp channel every 20 seconds and answers questions from the contacts allowed below.
whatsapp.forget_pairing_hint: The next start of the bridge prints a new QR code. Say why.
whatsapp.no_contacts: No contacts yet. Add the CEO below.
whatsapp.number_hint: International format with the plus: +9647xxxxxxxxx. A local 07xx number is read as Iraq.
whatsapp.queries_note: Questions are answered only for a user who holds the CEO role and whose contact allows them; everybody else gets no reply. Every question runs read-only under that user’s own permissions and is written to the audit trail.
whatsapp.rules_note: A rule with the whatsapp channel sends to every recipient of its role who has an active contact with notifications allowed. The in-app copy always exists; a phone that cannot be reached is marked suppressed, never an error.
whatsapp.setting_agent_model: Agent model (reserved for the WA-3 agent)
whatsapp.setting_inline_rows: Rows shown as text before a file is attached
whatsapp.setting_export_rows_cap: Most rows in one attached file
whatsapp.setting_digest_locale: Language of the morning digest (ar or en)
whatsapp.settings_note: Models are Anthropic model ids; the bridge needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY on its host to use them, otherwise the phrase patterns alone route. Changes take effect on the bridge’s next poll.
whatsapp.actions_note: Deciding a document from chat needs this switch, an approval already waiting for that person, the written command (approve / reject) and the six-digit code sent back. The decision then runs under their own permissions, where the maker-checker rule and the open period refuse exactly as they do on the screen.
whatsapp.setting_group_queries: Answer questions in the group (on / off)
whatsapp.setting_group_notifications: Post notifications to the group (on / off)
whatsapp.setting_group_digest: Post the morning digest to the group (on / off)
whatsapp.group_hint: One group, by its id. Add the bot to the group, run "npm run whatsapp-bridge -- --list-groups", and paste the id here. Any other group is ignored.

projects.title: Project Master
projects.subtitle: Every project with a beginning, an end, a budget and somebody answerable for it — customer, internal or investment — with the five amounts summed from the rows each time.
projects.contracts_subtitle: Customer projects seen as contracts: value, billing method, retention and advance, what has been billed.
projects.wbs_subtitle: The work breakdown structure: each element coded by the mask, saying whether it may be planned, posted to and billed, with the amounts rolled up the tree.
projects.code_hint: Leave blank for the next number in the PRJ series; type a code the company already uses.
projects.contract_value_hint: Customer projects only; measured in IQD.
projects.no_projects: No project to show. Create one on Project Master.
projects.is_planning: Planning element — costs may be planned here
projects.is_account_assignment: Account-assignment element — costs, commitments and issues may be posted here
projects.is_billing: Billing element — certificates and the billing plan hang here
projects.wbs_code_hint: Leave blank for the next number under the parent (the coding mask: PRJ-…-1, -1.2, -1.2.3).
projects.deactivate_note: A deactivated element keeps its history and receives nothing new. It is refused while it carries budget, costs or active children.
projects.activate_note: Reactivating the element lets it receive plans and costs again.
projects.budgets_subtitle: The budget as documents: the original, supplements, returns and transfers between elements — raised by one person, approved by another. The budget by element is the sum of the approved ones.
projects.change_order_lines_note: Type the budget the change adds on each element and cost code; a negative figure takes budget away. Approved twice, the change order raises the supplement itself.
projects.change_orders_subtitle: Variations with their scope, cost and schedule effect — a commercial and a budget approval, neither by the raiser; the baseline never moves.
projects.contract_delta_hint: What the customer's contract value moves by; negative for a reduction.
projects.four_eyes_note: You raised this document; somebody else approves it.
projects.has_original: {code} already has its original budget — raise a supplement, a return or a transfer.
projects.kind_original_hint: The first budget of the project: it writes the baseline, once.
projects.kind_supplement_hint: Adds budget to elements; the baseline stays.
projects.kind_return_hint: Takes budget back from elements that will not need it.
projects.kind_transfer_hint: Moves budget between elements; the project's total does not change.
projects.kind_original_lines: One amount per element and cost code. Leave a cell blank for nothing.
projects.kind_supplement_lines: One amount per element and cost code to add. Leave a cell blank for nothing.
projects.kind_return_lines: Type what is taken back from each element and cost code, as a positive figure.
projects.kind_transfer_lines: A negative figure on the element that gives, a positive one on the element that receives; the lines sum to zero.
projects.new_budget_subtitle: Name the project, choose the kind, and type one amount per element and cost code.
projects.new_change_order_subtitle: Name the project, describe the change, and type the budget it moves element by element.
projects.no_budget_lines: No budget lines by cost code yet — the original budget's approval writes them.
projects.no_budget_moved: This change order moves no budget.
projects.no_plan_lines: Nothing planned in this version yet.
projects.no_plan_yet: No plan yet — a version is created first.
projects.no_planning_elements: The project has no active planning element.
projects.older_version: an older version, kept as it was
projects.pick_project: Type the project's code or name and choose it.
projects.plan_subtitle: The cost plan by element, cost code and month, in versions — the original and the re-plans; the current one is what earned value reads.
projects.position_note: The baseline beside the revised figures — the baseline never moves.
projects.project_ambiguous: More than one project matches — type more of its code or name.
projects.revised_ends_on_hint: A date, when the change sets one; else the days above move the forecast finish.
projects.schedule_delta_hint: Days added to the forecast finish; negative for earlier.
projects.scope_note_hint: What changes in the work, in a few lines.
projects.set_month_note: One cell of the plan: the element, the cost code and the month; the amount replaces what was there.
projects.set_month_title: Set one month of the plan
projects.spread_note: The total is spread evenly from the first month to the last; the remainder lands on the last month so the sum is exact.
projects.stop_line_hint: Percent of the element's budget; blank restores the profile's line.
projects.stop_line_note: The profile stops at {percent} %. A project manager may raise the line to 110 %; beyond that the accounting manager raises it. The reason is recorded.
projects.supersedes_hint: The approved change order this one replaces, when it does.
projects.version_note: A new version becomes the current one; older versions are kept as they were.
projects.costs_subtitle: The line items: every cost on a project with its element, cost code, document and journal — the sum beside the ledger's figure.
projects.issue_note: One item per document, as a stock transfer: the issue leaves the warehouse at FIFO cost when the document is posted; a return goes back at the cost typed.
projects.journal_reconciliation: Line items {items} · journal lines with the dimension {journal}
projects.material_issues_subtitle: Stock issued from a warehouse to an element at layer cost, or returned at the cost it went out at.
projects.no_procurement: No order or payable is assigned to a project element yet.
projects.procurement_subtitle: The orders and payables assigned to project elements: the promise each one made, what became actual, what was given back, what is still open.
projects.stock_at_issue_note: goods bought for the project are stock until a material issue takes them to the element
projects.unit_cost_hint: A return names the cost the stock went out at; an issue takes the layer's.
projects.wbs_filter_hint: An element's code; its children are included.
projects.activity_code_hint: Leave blank for the next code (A0010, A0020, …).
projects.actual_note: What happened: the day the work began, how far it has gone, and the day it finished.
projects.cancel_activity_note: A cancelled activity stays on the record and leaves the schedule; its links stop counting.
projects.duration_hint: Working days in the project's calendar; a milestone has none.
projects.evm_note: Planned from the current plan; earned from approved progress × budget; actual from the costs — each to the day, summed up the tree before the ratios are taken.
projects.measure_note: Somebody other than you approves the measurement before it counts.
projects.not_before_hint: The earliest day it may start (a milestone: the day it stands at).
projects.progress_percent_hint: For a progress milestone: the element's percent when it is reached.
projects.progress_subtitle: Earned value element by element — plan, earned, actual, CPI, SPI, EAC — with the measurements, the milestones and their trend.
projects.schedule_note: The critical path is worked out from the links and the calendar: earliest and latest dates, float, and the critical activities; each milestone's date is kept for the trend.
projects.trend_note: Each milestone's date at every schedule run
projects.baseline_fixed: The project is released: the baseline is written once. A change in scope, value or dates is a change order.
projects.no_budget: No budget lines yet — they arrive with the budget documents (Stage PM-2).
projects.balances_note: Retention and the advance are balances of their own, not revenue
projects.billing_line_note: A milestone line falls due when its billing milestone is reached and approved; a date line on its date. The plan never bills more than the contract value as it stands.
projects.billing_subtitle: The billing plan, the certificates raised from it, the contract balances and the period's revenue recognition
projects.billing_value_hint: A percentage of the contract (e.g. 30) or an amount in IQD
projects.certificate_posting_note: Approved by somebody other than its raiser, the certificate posts: the customer's receivable (gross less retention), the retention receivable and the contract revenue (gross), on its own date.
projects.certify_percent_hint: The cumulative percentage of the contract — never beyond approved measured progress
projects.certify_progress_note: The certificate bills what the percentage reaches less what is already certified; retention is withheld and the advance recovered on the project's terms.
projects.etc_note: The latest estimate dated on or before the report's day replaces the formula for that element; each is kept with its reason.
projects.forecast_subtitle: Per element: plan, budget, committed, actual, estimate to complete, estimate at completion and variance
projects.no_customer_projects: There is no customer project to bill.
projects.no_typed_etc: No estimate has been typed; the formula stands.
projects.recognition_after_release: Recognition starts once the project is released.
projects.recognition_not_ratified: The recognition method is not yet ratified by Finance (D-PM-1). The figures are what would post; nothing posts until it is ratified on Project Settings.
projects.recognition_onerous: The estimate at completion exceeds the contract value: this is a loss contract. A provision for the loss is Finance's judgement and is not posted here.
projects.recognition_ratified: Percentage of completion, cost to cost — ratified by {by}: {note}. The run posts recognised less billed at the period end and is reversed on the first day of the next run.
projects.book_hours_note: Booked by one person, approved by another, and posted by Finance once the month has ended — at the base salary in force ÷ the calendar's working days ÷ 8 (D-PM-8).
projects.close_checks_meta: {count, plural, =0 {nothing stands in the way} one {# thing stands in the way} other {# things stand in the way}}
projects.close_project_note: Closed is final: the project and its elements refuse every posting from now on.
projects.close_subtitle: Technical completion, settlement to the asset or the result, and the close — with everything that stands in the way
projects.hours_hint: Up to 24 a day across all projects, e.g. 7.5
projects.kind_of_customer: Customer project — settles to the result
projects.kind_of_internal: Internal project — settles to the result
projects.kind_of_investment: Investment project — settles to the asset under construction
projects.reports_subtitle: The hierarchy cost report, the line items, the milestone trend and earned value — printed and exported as the screen shows them
projects.settlement_asset_note: An investment project's cost leaves the expense accounts it was posted to for the asset under construction; the asset is capitalised on the Fixed Assets screen. Drafted by one person, posted by another.
projects.settlement_result_note: The revenue recognition still standing is reversed, so WIP and deferred revenue are clear and the result stays in the P&L. Drafted by one person, posted by another.
projects.technical_complete_note: No new commitment or issue is accepted after this; the cost of work already done, the final billing and the settlement still are.

project_settings.title: Project Settings
project_settings.subtitle: Project types, tolerance profiles and cost codes — rows an administrator edits. Nothing deletes; a row is deactivated.
project_settings.kind_internal: Internal — cost only, settles to the result
project_settings.kind_investment: Investment — settles to a fixed asset
project_settings.profile_note: Availability control reads the project’s profile: at the warning line the responsible person and the project manager are told; at the stop line the commitment or posting is refused.
project_settings.method_poc_cost_to_cost: Percentage of completion, cost to cost, at period end
project_settings.recognition_note: Recognised revenue to date is the contract value × actual cost ÷ estimate at completion; the period journal posts the difference from what was billed to WIP or deferred revenue and is reversed next period (D-PM-1). Nothing posts until Finance ratifies the method.
project_settings.ratify_hint: The decision this rests on — e.g. the Finance committee minute

bank_deposits.subtitle: Money put into a bank account by hand — cash taken to the bank, or money from any other source. Each is approved by somebody else and posted.
bank_deposits.new_cash_note: Cash taken from one of the company’s cash accounts to the bank: a bank transfer, Dr the bank, Cr the cash.
bank_deposits.new_other_note: Money from outside the company’s own accounts — capital, a refund, a sale outside the ledgers: Dr the bank, Cr the account it was for (never a control account).

availability.subtitle: What each warehouse holds, item by item: on hand, available to issue, and what is reserved, in transit, in quarantine, damaged or returned — every figure summed from the stock ledger.
availability.issue_note: Takes stock out of the warehouse at FIFO cost. An issue larger than what is available is refused, with the figures.

hr_structure.departments_subtitle: Every department, its people and its seats. A department is the company's one list — the same the ledger's department dimension names.
hr_structure.name: Name
hr_structure.seats_none: No position is set up in this department yet.
hr_structure.people_none: Nobody works in this department yet.
hr_structure.positions_subtitle: The seats of the organisation: the title, the department, who it reports to and who holds it. The code is minted.
hr_structure.reports_none: No position reports to this one.

profile.title: My profile
profile.change_password_hint: Enter your current password, then the new one twice. Your other sessions will be signed out.
profile.new_password_hint: At least 12 characters. A few words are easier to remember and harder to guess.
profile.avatar_hint: PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 400 KB. A square image looks best.
profile.temporary_hint: You signed in with a temporary password. Choose your own before continuing; nothing else is available until you do.
profile.mfa_required_hint: This account signs in with an authenticator code. Enrol one below.
profile.mfa_grace: This account must enrol an authenticator by {date}. After that date it can do nothing else until it has.
profile.mfa_grace_over: The enrolment period has passed. Enrol an authenticator now; nothing else is available until you do.
profile.mfa_begin_hint: Install an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, Aegis…). Begin shows a key to add to it; the app’s first code confirms it.
profile.mfa_replace_hint: Replacing issues a new key. Until the new app confirms it, sign-in needs the code from the old one.
profile.mfa_confirm_title: Add the key to your app, then confirm
profile.mfa_confirm_hint: In the app choose “enter a setup key” and type the key, or paste the otpauth address. Then enter the six-digit code the app shows.
profile.mfa_enrolled: The authenticator is enrolled. Sign-in will ask for its code.

event.sales_customer_receipt_identified: Customer Receipt — put to a customer
event.purchasing_supplier_advance_settlement: Supplier advance applied to an invoice

role.supplier_payable: What the company owes the supplier
role.expense: The cost of a service billed
role.purchase_variance: The difference between the order and the invoice
role.customer_receivable: What the customer owes the company
role.customer_clearing: Money received, not yet put to a customer
role.opening_balance: What the opening stock is opened against
role.inventory_adjustment: Stock found or lost on reconciliation
role.landed_cost_clearing: A cost charged to an import, until its landed cost is locked
role.loan_liability: What the company owes the bank on the loan
role.bank_commission: The bank’s commission, when it is expensed
role.project_retention_receivable: Retention the customer holds until release
role.project_deferred_revenue: Billed ahead of the work (deferred revenue)
role.supplier_advance: Money paid to suppliers ahead of the invoice (advances)
role.bank: The bank or cash account, when none is named

print.too_many_rows: This export has {rows} rows; a file may carry at most {cap}. Narrow the filters (a shorter period, one item or one warehouse) and export again.
print.no_allocations: Not allocated to any invoice yet.
